LESSON: WRITING 1.4.1 SENTENCE FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Writing 1.4.1 Sentence fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.4.1 Sentence fluency, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What can make a sentence confusing to a reader? 2. Why should we write complete sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work together to pick out sentences that are well punctuated with the comma. Learners with speech difficulties could point/type or answer orally,

2. research sentences featuring a misused comma correctly: comma splices, run on sentences, and run on lines (in online and offline passages) Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work together to pick out sentences that are well punctuated with the comma. Learners with speech difficulties could point/type or answer orally,
2. research sentences featuring a misused comma correctly: comma splices, run on sentences, and run on lines (in online and offline passages) Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.4.1 Sentence fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy as the learner determines the success criteria when they exchange the sentences created for peer review.

● Learning to learn as the learner learns independently as they research sentences featuring a misused comma correctly.

Values

● Respect is promoted as the learner exhibits humility as they exchange the sentences created for peer review.

● Integrity is enhanced as the learner displays honesty as they search online and offline for passages with comma splices,

run on sentences and run on lines without visiting undesirable sites.
